events.title: Yom Kippur War Begins
events.description: Egypt and Syria launched a coordinated surprise attack on Israeli positions in the Sinai Peninsula and Golan Heights on Yom Kippur, the holiest day in Judaism, which in 1973 coincided with Ramadan.
events.significance: The war led to an Arab oil embargo, a global energy crisis, superpower tensions, and eventually the Camp David Accords and the 1979 Egypt-Israel peace treaty.

events.title: Assassination of Anwar Sadat
events.description: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat was assassinated by Islamist militants within the army while watching a military parade in Cairo commemorating the 1973 war.
events.significance: Sadat's death removed a key Arab architect of peace with Israel and led Hosni Mubarak to power, who ruled Egypt for nearly three decades.

events.title: Premiere of The Jazz Singer
events.description: Warner Bros. premiered The Jazz Singer, starring Al Jolson, in New York City. It was the first feature-length film with synchronized dialogue and singing sequences.
events.significance: The film marked the beginning of the end of the silent film era and the rise of 'talkies' in the motion picture industry.

events.title: William Tyndale Executed
events.description: English scholar William Tyndale was strangled and burned at the stake for heresy near Brussels after translating the New Testament into English.
events.significance: His translation strongly influenced later English Bibles, including the King James Version, and shaped the English language and the Reformation in England.

events.title: Moulin Rouge Opens in Paris
events.description: The Moulin Rouge cabaret opened in the Montmartre district of Paris, introducing its distinctive red windmill and popularizing the can-can dance.
events.significance: It became a symbol of Parisian nightlife and the Belle Époque, inspiring artists such as Toulouse-Lautrec.
